Let the storefront do the storefront: Discovery, search and a published catalog are real work, and none of it happens here. The accounts who want to browse keep browsing. The ones who just want Friday's order reordered get a quicker route to it.
Money and paperwork stay put: VOS never touches money. Nothing about adding it asks you to move how customers pay or how invoices go out, which is usually the part nobody wants to disturb.
Still one place for the order to arrive: Whichever system you picked is where it shows up, over EDI, the API or QuickBooks. So nobody is watching two queues.

@graph.name: Is VOS a fair Cut+Dry alternative, and is it better than Cut+Dry?

acceptedAnswer.text: On order capture, yes to both, and that is the comparison worth making: a reorder from an account you already have arrives with no browsing, nobody promoting into it, and go-live in a day or two for most. Everywhere else they are not the same purchase. Cut+Dry runs a storefront, takes payments, raises invoices and carries a sales tool, and VOS moves one order from your account to your desk. One of those is a platform decision and one is not.

@graph.name: Can another brand advertise to my customer inside VOS?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. There is no advertising surface in the app, and we do not sell placement to anyone. Your account sees your own range, priced the way you hold it. Cut+Dry openly offers manufacturers targeted marketing at the moment an operator is ordering, which suits some distributors and is exactly what others are avoiding.

@graph.name: Does VOS do payments or invoicing?

acceptedAnswer.text: Neither. Money never passes through it. If digital payments and automated invoicing are what you are shopping for, that is a genuine Cut+Dry strength and we would point you back to them for it.

@graph.name: Does any of this touch our ERP?

acceptedAnswer.text: Only to hand it the order. VOS works at the intake end and passes each one on, itemized and approved. Everything downstream behaves exactly as it did yesterday.

Neither of us publishes a figure. They have a pricing page with no prices on it, and ours comes as a quote and is not on the site either. Given the difference in scope, the thing to compare is not the number but what each number is buying.

@graph.name: How quickly can accounts start sending orders?

acceptedAnswer.text: For most distributors this is live inside 24 to 48 hours, with a first order usually in on the same day. Cut+Dry publishes "Go Live in Under 90 Days" on their own distributor page, which is respectable for a platform that size and still most of a quarter, and the common reason a Cut+Dry alternative gets weighed at all.

@graph.name: And the accounts that will only ever call?

acceptedAnswer.text: They carry on calling, and your desk deals with those the way it always has. Be clear about the limit though: a call or a voicemail gets no order number from VOS, no timestamp and nothing moving in stock. Only what comes through the app does.

@graph.name: Where do the Cut+Dry details on this page come from?

acceptedAnswer.text: All of the above was read on their own site, 10 October 2026: the module descriptions, the manufacturer marketing pitch, the cashback offer and the published 90 day launch, and the named customer they credit it to. We have left their growth percentages alone, because those are their numbers. If any of it has moved on, the fault is here, not there.
